story.headline: Cursor Projects beta lets website or app work continue online after your laptop closes.

heroVisual.alt: Illustration of a magnifying glass examining the evidence behind an AI headline in a newspaper.

story.the_story:
Cursor launched Projects in beta on September 10 for longer software jobs, from adding a feature to building a whole app. A Project keeps the files and notes for that job, so agents working on different parts can use what the others have learned. A coordinator is the agent that plans the job and sends pieces to other agents; Cursor says the other agents write the code.

A Project runs on a computer in the cloud—online rather than on your laptop—so closing your laptop does not stop that part of the job. If testing is needed on your own computer, Cursor says the coordinator starts a local agent there. The result comes back to you to check.
story.laidies_read:
For your own website, ask before you start: can the remaining work stay online, or does a test need your laptop? That determines whether closing it will interrupt the job.

Projects are in beta and rolling out to all users.
story.what_this_means: When the page comes back, check the thing you asked for: does it say what you meant, do its links work, and did anything else change? That is the concrete job that still belongs to you.
story.cocktail_party: “Cursor Projects can keep cloud work moving after your laptop closes; testing on your own computer is a separate local-agent handoff.”
story.class_notes: AI Fundamentals 101: Agents — AI That Acts explains agents that plan, use tools, and keep state across steps—the pieces behind Cursor’s coordinator and handoffs.

universalAnswers.whatHappened: Cursor launched Projects in beta on September 10.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: A Project is a continuing workspace for a larger job, with one coordinator agent assigning pieces to other agents.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: Cursor’s September 10 changelog provides the beta, coordinator, cloud/local, context, and rollout statements.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: The vendor announcement does not establish output quality, permissions, reader uptake, or a result for a particular project.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: A reader building a personal site/app or coordinating a larger work project may want a job to continue with context rather than restart as a fresh chat.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: Projects are rolling out to Cursor users; the announcement gives no claim about suitability for every user or job.
universalAnswers.changesNow: Cursor says Projects are in beta and rolling out to all users starting September 10.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: The release does not promise that agents produce correct work or explain what access any local task may require.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Decide whether you have a bounded longer job you can inspect after the coordinator returns work.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: Is this a continuing, inspectable job with a clear result, or am I expecting an agent to replace my review?

model-tool-release.nearestAlternatives: The stated contrast is a Project retaining context over a job instead of repeatedly onboarding an agent for each task.
model-tool-release.availability: Projects are in beta and rolling out to all users starting September 10.
model-tool-release.freePaidBoundary: The announcement does not state a free or paid boundary.
model-tool-release.costBoundary: The announcement does not state pricing or cost effects.
model-tool-release.limitations: The provider gives no quality guarantee, permission description, or result for a reader’s particular job.
model-tool-release.technicalExampleProportionality: The coordinator/local-agent explanation is kept to the stated planning, delegation, cloud, and testing handoff.
